components.css: .ds-product { width: 250px; color: #334155; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-product-image { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; aspect-ratio: 4/3; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 12px; background: #f3f4f6; color: #94a3b8; font-size: 12px; transition: transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-product:hover .ds-product-image { transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-product-image button { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.9); color: #64748b; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / .12); font-size: 20px; } .ds-product-image button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(245,158,11,.35); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-product-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-top: 8px; color: #f59e0b; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .025em; } .ds-product-meta span { border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 8px; font-size: 10px; } .ds-product h3 { margin: 4px 0; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-product strong { color: #b45309; font-size: 20px; }

narrative.overview:
The Golden Lens presents optical retail through warmth, clarity, and measured polish. Amber communicates care and value, slate supplies professional restraint, and generous white or cream surfaces keep product photography and practical information easy to read. The result should feel refined, calm, and professional rather than clinical or luxurious for its own sake.

The interface is softly layered: fine borders establish most structure, while restrained shadows lift menus, interactive cards, and important actions. Rounded forms make commerce and service workflows reassuring without becoming playful. Zen Antique appears selectively as a warm editorial accent; the system sans serif carries navigation, product data, forms, checkout, and administrative work.
keyCharacteristics: Warm amber hierarchy against quiet slate neutrals
Product-led imagery with calm, readable supporting UI
Fine borders first, soft elevation second
Selective display typography paired with practical system text

rules.name: The Amber Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Bright, core, and deep amber tones must communicate increasing emphasis; do not use them interchangeably as decoration.

rules.name: The Quiet Canvas Rule
rules.body: Product imagery and transactional content sit on white, cream, or mist-slate surfaces so the merchandise remains the visual lead.

rules.name: The Selective Serif Rule
rules.body: Zen Antique is an accent for meaningful customer-facing moments, not the default for dense forms, navigation, prices, or administration.

rules.name: The Readable Commerce Rule
rules.body: Functional text remains in the system sans serif, with semibold weight used to signal action or hierarchy rather than ornamental styling.

rules.name: The Product Breathing Room Rule
rules.body: Dense data can remain compact, but product imagery, major services, and checkout decisions must keep clear separation and stable alignment.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Establish structure with a fine border or tonal shift first; add a shadow only when an element needs to sit above its surroundings.

rules.name: The Reassuring Curve Rule
rules.body: Corners should feel soft and deliberate; do not mix square and highly rounded elements within the same component family without a functional reason.

dos: Do use Optician's Amber for the primary commercial action and price emphasis.
Do keep most surfaces white, Amber Cream, or Mist Slate so products and service information remain clear.
Do use thin borders and tonal shifts before adding elevation.
Do reserve Zen Antique for selective customer-facing headlines and service moments.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, readable contrast, and scalable text across customer journeys.
donts: Don't turn the amber family into undifferentiated decoration; every shade must carry a clear hierarchy role.
Don't use heavy shadows on every card or control; elevation is a response to hierarchy and interaction.
Don't apply the display serif to dense product data, forms, checkout, or administrative interfaces.
Don't let decorative overlays overpower product photography or reduce text contrast.
Don't introduce sharp, clinical geometry into an otherwise rounded and reassuring component family.
